tldr: A transition is a second job you do without pay, on top of the first one. Decide how many hours a week it gets, split them on purpose, and start the heavy applying at least six to eight weeks before the date you could start a new job.

blocks.text: Give the search fixed hours every week

Decide how many hours a week the search gets, then split them six parts proof, three parts people and one part reading. Documented SLP transitions took six to fifteen months, which is too long to run on leftover evenings, so treat the search like a caseload: fixed hours, a schedule, and something written down at the end of each week. Keep the proportions even when the total changes. Most people do it backwards, with ten parts reading and a search that never leaves the browser.

items.title: Three parts people
items.text: Messages and calls with people who hold the title you want.

items.title: One part reading
items.text: Articles, postings and forums, kept to the smallest share.

blocks.text: Count back from the day you could start a new job

Start applying hard at least six to eight weeks before the earliest date you could start. Interviews take weeks and two weeks' notice is the convention, so a start date usually falls two to four weeks after an offer. That window is the latest you can begin, and the documented searches below ran for months, so begin earlier if you can. Everything before it is proof and conversations, the work that makes applications land.

blocks.text: Some states set a last penalty-free day to resign that falls weeks before the first day of school, and resigning after it can carry a penalty. Read your contract and your state's rule before you agree to a start date.
Plan for more applications than feels reasonable

One documented SLP sent 113 tailored applications over eleven months for seven interviews and one offer, and another sent more than five hundred in six months. At one application a week, 113 takes more than two years, so the calendar has to hold a faster pace than that. Lesson 6.6 walks through both searches.

blocks.title: Let an alert watch the boards
blocks.text: Applications sent in the first day or two of a posting are the ones most likely to be seen. Set a job alert for your target title so new postings come to you, and check it in one short slot a day once your applying window opens.

All six on applications, because volume is what counts

The map sorts paths by how long they take, because time is what you are short of. Choose the tier by what your bank account and your patience will carry: the top one hires on the license in your wallet, and the bottom one has the highest ceilings and the longest wait.
The only thing preventing me from leaving the field is not knowing what else I can do as a career.

blocks.text: Four jobs hire you on the license you already hold

Clinical liaison, utilization review, clinical educator and case management all ask for a clinician, and you are one: no bootcamp, no portfolio, no year of evenings. Clinical liaison gets called the number one non-clinical title for rehab professionals. State Disability Determination Services is a second door into review work, and one SLP took a $13,000 pay cut to walk through it for the mobility and a PSLF-qualifying employer.

items.title: Clinical or rehab liaison
items.text: You read charts between a hospital and a rehab facility to judge who fits your program. Encompass Health, Select Medical and Lifepoint all hire for it.

items.title: Utilization review
items.text: You read a request for care against the criteria that decide payment, then write the decision. Remote-heavy and fast to enter.

items.title: Clinical educator or trainer
items.text: You train clinicians, families and school teams on a device you already prescribe. Tobii Dynavox calls it Learning Consultant. PRC-Saltillo, Lingraphica and Passy-Muir hire the same profile.

items.title: Case management
items.text: You coordinate care across settings, insurers and discharge. $54,100 to $81,900 in the middle band, with government near $82,600 and insurance near $80,500 at the median.

items: Clinical or rehab liaison

Clinical educator or trainer

items: You are still inside acute care most days, and part of the job is selling.
You often say no to clinicians who sound like you, and many postings want an RN.
Travel. Find the percentage in the posting before you fall in love with the job.

blocks.text: 100% remote (a literal dream for me)

blocks.title: Picture the Wednesday before you apply
blocks.text: All four keep you inside the system you are leaving, and that is the trade. Picture an ordinary Wednesday in one of them: same building, same acronyms, same people, different badge, no caseload. If that reads as relief, this tier is your fastest way out and you can apply this month. If it reads as a halfway house, spend your evenings on the later tiers and take the longer road on purpose.

items: Search "clinical liaison" and "utilization review" with your state, and read the first five postings end to end.

blocks.text: Most SLPs who leave land in one of these four clusters

Customer success, project management, healthcare data and content are where documented SLP exits keep landing. Customer success has the best effort-to-odds ratio on the map, and at Expressable, Presence, Tobii Dynavox, PRC-Saltillo, Lingraphica and Passy-Muir your license is the credential. None of the four is quick: the data analyst below sent more than five hundred applications before an offer came.

items.title: Customer success and implementation
items.text: You teach clinicians to use a product, then keep them using it. $75,000 to $120,000. The first vocabulary is churn, onboarding and health scores.

items.title: Project and program management
items.text: A caseload is concurrent projects with worse tooling. This cluster has the most six-figure outcomes on file.

items.title: Healthcare data
items.text: $70,000 to $105,000. Start at healthcare organizations and not big tech: hospital quality teams working falls data and discharge follow-up, behavioral health organizations, payers.

items.title: Content and marketing
items.text: The skill is explaining a swallow study to a frightened spouse in words he can act on. $80,000 to $141,000, and income is lumpy at the beginning.

items.label: medical SLP to remote SaaS customer success manager

items: SLP to IT project manager
SLP to project manager
SLP to hospital data analyst
SLP to corporate marketing

right.label: The numbers
items: Six figures, double the SLP salary, after fifteen months and six interviews across three rounds
About $90,000 salaried eighteen months in, after $38 to $48 an hour as a clinician
A one-year online master's while working, then the same salary as the last SLP job
About a year of applications, then a raise and a bonus

**Customer success.** The $115,000 to $120,000 manager was a medical SLP who went through SV Academy's free customer success bootcamp and a paid internship. SV Academy now advertises sales development training, so check what it offers today.

**Project management.** Another SLP was an associate PM inside a year. The Google certificate is low-cost, and PMI's CAPM and PMP fees change, so check pmi.org before you budget. PMI counts time spent leading defined projects toward the PMP, and routine caseload work does not count. One SLP who moved wrote, "no one took me seriously with a CAPM."

**Healthcare data.** The remote analyst had about ten years, mostly in early intervention, and got there through thirteen interview processes and four finals, self-taught, with free and low-cost certificates and a five-project portfolio. The master's route started $15,000 below that SLP's peak home-health year, with guaranteed annual raises and 85k+ after the entry level.

**Content and marketing.** The marketer wrote, "I actually got a raise and bonus this year, whereas in my 5 years in healthcare I was given a .35 cent raise." Another SLP started freelance with a single $200 article on Upwork and now runs a micro-agency.

blocks.text: Apply one title below the job you want
The door that opens first is one title below the job you want. Freelance counts as a door in content and in data, and one $200 article is a legitimate first line on a portfolio.

Pick the cluster whose bad day you could live with, not the one whose good day sounds best.

blocks.text: Count the months before you start a path that takes a year or more

The long builds have the highest ceilings, and you pay for them in evenings: five to eight hours a week, after the last note is written, for six months to two years. BLS puts the SLP median at $97,870, well below the top of this tier. Lesson 2.5 explains the gates on Epic certification and UX research.

items.label: healthtech UX research, the realistic niche
one self-taught SLP software engineer, starting pay and after two years

items.title: Clinical informatics and EHR
items.text: Six to eighteen months. The superuser who fixes everyone's templates has done this unpaid for years. CAHIMS from HIMSS is the credential you can buy yourself.

items.title: Instructional design
items.text: Six to twelve months, $70,000 to $100,000. The cost is three to five samples in Articulate Storyline 360 or Rise, each with a short process write-up. Spec work counts.

items.title: Conversation design
items.text: Glassdoor puts conversational designer at $68,000 to $101,800, average $82,700, and IT-sector median total pay at $96,900. The conversation designer title averages around $63,000.

items.title: UX research
items.text: Healthtech is the realistic niche, because clinical fluency is the part most candidates cannot fake. The cost is two to four deep case studies.

items.title: Software engineering
items.text: One to two years of self-teaching. One SLP started from $26 and $34 an hour in two part-time jobs. Another reached $96,000 self-taught.

items: **Informatics.** One widely read exit post was this move: eight years in acute care and a skilled nursing facility, then a clinical analyst role at the same hospital system, hybrid, $10,000 more. The poster had finished a second master's and still wrote, in capitals, that you do not need one.

**Instructional design.** No degree or certificate is required, so skip the paid certificate and build your samples from trainings you have already delivered. Learn the vocabulary instead: ADDIE, Kirkpatrick levels, Mayer's principles, andragogy.

**Conversation design.** You write what a voice assistant says and how it recovers when a person says something unexpected. Most roles sit inside big tech and consultancies such as Amazon, Meta and Accenture, so the search is national.
**UX research.** The standard for a case study is higher than it looks: "One honest case study including the wrong turns is worth more than six polished AI case studies."

**Software.** The first of those engineers held part-time jobs at a skilled nursing facility and a hospital, taught herself with free online courses, and was found by a recruiter on LinkedIn. This runway is the longest on the map and the least forgiving of a stop-start schedule.

blocks.title: Count the cost in months, using your worst week
blocks.text: Six to eighteen months for informatics, six to twelve for instructional design, a year or more for UX research, and one to two years for software. Pick the number of hours a week you can give it on a bad week, and do the multiplication before you pay for anything. If the answer runs past the date you set in lesson 0.2, take a fast-tier job first and build this from inside it, on a salary, with your evenings back.

items: Pick one path from this tier and write down the hours a week you can give it in a bad week.

Do that first step this week and notice whether you resent it. That reaction is the cheapest data you will get.

tldr: You cannot buy an Epic certification, medical science liaison is gated behind a doctorate, and UX research is oversaturated. All three have a real route behind them, and all three have somebody selling the shortcut.

blocks.text: You can only get Epic certified through an employer

Epic does not sell certification to individuals, so anyone selling you an Epic cert is selling something else with that word on the label. A sponsoring employer, usually a health system that runs Epic, pays for the training. One SLP on file became an Epic application analyst, and the most-read forum account of the move was internal, from the clinical floor into the same hospital system's analyst team. Go-live and consulting postings often ask for experience first, so read each one for what it wants. CAHIMS from HIMSS is the credential you can buy for yourself, and it asks for no health IT job first.

blocks.title: The route to a sponsored Epic certification

items.label: Superuser work
items.note: templates, rollouts, the colleague everyone asks

items.label: A sponsor-track role
items.note: junior analyst, go-live support, or a firm like Nordic or Tegria

blocks.text: Aim at clinical liaison, because medical science liaison wants a doctorate

Medical science liaison roles are effectively gated behind a PhD, PharmD or MD, and a clinical master's plus a certificate will not clear that gate. Clinical or rehab liaison at $84,000 to $135,000 is the accessible cousin, where your credential is sufficient and entry is fast. If you want the pharma side specifically, the documented route runs through clinical research, and the coordinator step is the one place on the map where a pay cut is expected.

blocks.title: One SLP's documented route into pharma

blocks.text: Go through healthtech if you still want UX research

UX graduate output grew about 35% in five years while openings stayed flat, which is why the field reads as open in blog posts and closed in your inbox. The SLP to UX research move rests on a single documented story, a rehab director who went through a bootcamp. If you still want it, the route is the healthtech niche at $67,000 to $154,000, and what decides it is two to four deep case studies with the wrong turns left in. Conversation design and instructional design sit next door and use most of the same skills.
Check three postings and two people before you pay for a credential

Each of these three has a real job, a real salary band, and a gate that the person selling the shortcut leaves out. One transitioner on file spent $220 on a résumé writer and $480 on a career coach, then paid for a teacher-transition program, before the thing that finally worked.

blocks.text: Let the report narrow the list when you cannot

The Pivot Report reads your résumé and returns the stage you are in, three paths with the first job title to apply for in each, and a thirty-day plan. A long map stalls a tired brain, and a burnt-out one most of all: one SLP described burnt-out brains as struggling with executive function at the moment a career change demands it.
It's so frustrating not knowing how to start.

blocks.text: Read your watch-out line twice

The useful line in your readiness profile is the watch-out, because the trap it names is usually one you have already walked into. The profile is one of four, and each comes with the trap it falls into and the strength it underrates. It describes how you are approaching the change and makes no claim about whether you are good enough.

items.title: Depleted expert
items.text: Needs a recovery-paced plan, and cannot see their own competence from where they are standing.

items.title: Quiet researcher
items.text: Has been reading for months, and needs permission more than information.

items.title: Restless builder
items.text: Has energy, four tabs open and no single target.

items.title: Ready leaper
items.text: Wants tactics and no more reassurance.

blocks.text: Argue with the ranking in writing

The report ranks paths on the evidence in your résumé, which is a different thing from what you want. Read the three in order and notice which one you argue with, because that reaction is data. If it puts clinical informatics first on the strength of an EMR rollout you barely remember, and you know you never want to open a chart again, write that down and take the second one.
Pick one target before you rewrite your résumé

Module 4 is where the list has to narrow to one path, because you translate your résumé for one target at a time and a résumé aimed at three jobs reads as aimed at none. Until then, try paths on: reopen the map in lesson 2.1, read the report's second and third paths, and argue with the ranking. The paths you set aside stay on the map.

items.q: Your report ranks clinical informatics first because of an EMR rollout you led, and you never want to open a chart again. What do you do?
options: Aim at informatics anyway, because the report ranks on evidence
Set the report aside and reread the whole map
Write down why it is wrong for you and take the second path
items.why: The report ranks on what your résumé shows, which is a different thing from what you want, so disagreeing with it in writing is a legitimate way to choose.

items.q: You like two of your three paths equally and Module 4 starts next week. How many targets does your résumé get?
options: One now, with the other kept as the next one to test
Both, in one résumé that covers each
Neither, until you are certain
items.why: A résumé aimed at more than one job reads as aimed at none, and the path you set aside stays on the map.
